title: Live-docs searches are reused, not paid again
goal: A research session that repeats a live docs search or fetch already made within the cache lifetime reads it from a local uncommitted cache instead of calling the docs server, and MCP output in this project is capped below the Claude Code default

gates.question: How long may a cached live-docs search or fetch be reused?
options: an on-disk cache keyed by server and query with a short lifetime
no cache: research reads the kb first and never repeats a search
gates.recommendation: an on-disk cache keyed by server and query with a short lifetime

notes: Baseline census: tool results of 314 transcripts of this project (52 sessions, 262 subagent runs), about 4 characters a token; each result is also re-read from cache on every later turn of its session. Per call: search_claude_code_docs about 26k characters, microsoft_docs_search about 22k, microsoft_docs_fetch about 10k, WebFetch about 7.5k; about 1.4M characters in all. No MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS in the project settings, so results ride the default cap and are paid in full; fetch.py's _cache serves source verification, not the docs servers; no PostToolUse hook trims MCP output. Kb facts: public/claude/tool-output-limits.md:12,18 (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS, anthropic/maxResultSizeChars, DOC S745 S740), public/claude/hooks.md:29,32 (updatedMCPToolOutput, DOC S743), public/agents/doc-lookup-sources.md:23 (DOC S2177), public/claude/otel-monitoring.md:18 (tool_result_size_bytes, DOC S744). The output cap alone is a small task; the cache is the saving.
